headline: Margin Collapses on Seasonal Deleverage; Turnaround Still Absent

highlights: Key Points  Revenue grew 6.5% YoY but declined 19.0% QoQ to Rs1,856mn, 4.1% above NBIE estimates.
The sequential decline reflects seasonality following the Apr–Jun back-to-school quarter.  Gross profit stood at Rs717mn, with margin at 38.6% (-556bps YoY/+339bps QoQ).

Easing crude-linked input costs supported sequential recovery, while the YoY decline reflects a high base of 44.2%.  EBITDA declined 46% YoY/44% QoQ to Rs87mn, 22.7% below our estimates, with margin at 4.7% (-458bps YoY/-214bps QoQ).

Despite gross-margin recovery, sticky employee and overhead costs amid lower sequential revenue resulted in adverse operating leverage.  PAT declined 67% YoY/65% QoQ to Rs26mn, 42.9% below our estimates.  We maintain Sell with a revised TP of Rs70 (from Rs76 earlier) and roll forward our valuation to 21x Sept’28E EPS.

Key Points  Revenue grew 6.5% YoY but declined 19.0% QoQ to Rs1,856mn, 4.1% above NBIE estimates. The sequential decline reflects seasonality following the Apr–Jun back-to-school quarter.  Gross profit stood at Rs717mn, with margin at 38.6% (-556bps YoY/+339bps QoQ). Easing crude-linked input costs supported sequential recovery, while the YoY decline reflects a high base of 44.2%.  EBITDA declined 46% YoY/44% QoQ to Rs87mn, 22.7% below our estimates, with margin at 4.7% (-458bps YoY/-214bps QoQ). Despite gross-margin recovery, sticky employee and overhead costs amid lower sequential revenue resulted in adverse operating leverage.  PAT declined 67% YoY/65% QoQ to Rs26mn, 42.9% below our estimates.  We maintain Sell with a revised TP of Rs70 (from Rs76 earlier) and roll forward our valuation to 21x Sept’28E EPS. Outlook: H1 earnings lag despite modest revenue growth: H1FY27 revenue grew 3.2% YoY to Rs4,148mn, while EBITDA/PAT declined 30.5%/45% to Rs248mn/Rs99mn, achieving ~49%/~54% of FY27E estimates. While H2 seasonality offers recovery potential, persistent cost rigidity limits earnings headroom and highlights weak conversion of revenue growth into profitability. Kokuyo Camlin's inability to generate operating leverage remains a key concern, with sticky overheads limiting the benefit of sequential gross-margin recovery. H1FY27 EBITDA margin of 6.0% remains materially below DOMS and Flair (~13–16%), highlighting the structural profitability gap. Continued market-share pressure in colours, art materials and geometry boxes further weighs on growth visibility. Valuation: We cut FY27E/FY28E EBITDA by 15.6%/8.3% and PAT by 26.6%/9.8%, respectively, factoring in persistent cost pressures and weaker operating leverage. We reiterate Sell and cut our TP to Rs70 at 21x Sept’28E EPS. At Cmp of Rs75 the stock trades at 42x FY27E and 23x FY28E EPS, valuations remain demanding given subdued growth, weak margins and low- teens RoCE. We prefer DOMS and Flair (both BUY) for stationery exposure. The core concern is Kokuyo Camlin's inability to convert its brand and distribution into consistent, profitable topline growth. Key monitorables include volume recovery, sustained input-cost relief, overhead rationalisation and potential parent-led initiatives to improve profitability.
